answer.en: Guided media carries signals through a physical, enclosed medium, while unguided media carries signals through free space without any physical medium (wireless).

title.ne: Group B - Q5: Dry run the given program

answer.en: Output: CMUE
answer.ne: Output: CMUE

solution.en: T$ = "COMPUTER" (length 8). The loop runs C = 1 to 8, STEP 2, so C takes the values 1, 3, 5, 7. Each time, D$ picks out a single character at position C using MID$(T$, C, 1), and PRINT D$; prints it without a line break. C=1 gives "C", C=3 gives "M", C=5 gives "U", C=7 gives "E", producing the final output CMUE.
solution.ne: T$ = "COMPUTER" (length 8). The loop runs C = 1 to 8, STEP 2, so C takes the values 1, 3, 5, 7. Each time, D$ picks out a single character at position C using MID$(T$, C, 1), and PRINT D$; prints it without a line break. C=1 gives "C", C=3 gives "M", C=5 gives "U", C=7 gives "E", producing the final output CMUE.

items.code:
DECLARE SUB Display (T$)
T$="COMPUTER"
CALL Display (T$)
END

SUB Display (T$)
  FOR C=1 TO LEN (T$) STEP 2
    D$=MID$ (T$,C,1)
    PRINT D$;
  NEXT C
END SUB

title.en: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program
title.ne: Group B - Q6: Correct the bugs in the given program

answer.en: The program has three bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement, and a mismatched GOTO label.
answer.ne: The program has three bugs: the file open mode, a write statement wrongly written as a read statement, and a mismatched GOTO label.

solution.en: (1) 'OPEN "student.dat" FOR OUT AS #2' is invalid QBASIC syntax and would also erase the existing file; since the comment says records should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #2'. (2) 'INPUT#2, SNames$,C,RN' reads from the file instead of writing to it, and also misspells the variable SName$ as SNames$; to add a record it must be 'PRINT #2, SName$, C, RN'. (3) The label is defined as 'TOP:' but the loop jumps to 'GOTO POP', which does not exist; it must jump back to 'GOTO TOP' to repeat the input loop.
solution.ne: (1) 'OPEN "student.dat" FOR OUT AS #2' is invalid QBASIC syntax and would also erase the existing file; since the comment says records should be added to an existing file, it must be 'FOR APPEND AS #2'. (2) 'INPUT#2, SNames$,C,RN' reads from the file instead of writing to it, and also misspells the variable SName$ as SNames$; to add a record it must be 'PRINT #2, SName$, C, RN'. (3) The label is defined as 'TOP:' but the loop jumps to 'GOTO POP', which does not exist; it must jump back to 'GOTO TOP' to repeat the input loop.

items.code:
REM to add record in an existing file.
OPEN "student.dat" FOR APPEND AS #2
TOP:
INPUT "Enter Name, Class and Roll No."; SName$, C, RN
PRINT #2, SName$, C, RN
INPUT "More records"; Y$
IF UCASE$(Y$) = "Y" THEN GOTO TOP
CLOSE #2
STOP

answer.en: PRINT COUNT(W$)

solution.en: The FUNCTION COUNT(A$) is declared and defined but never called in the main module, and its result is never displayed. The missing statement, placed after the INPUT line, is 'PRINT COUNT(W$)', which calls the function with the entered word and prints the number of vowels it returns. Note: this answer also assumes the printed 'MID$(C$,i,1)' inside the function should read 'MID$(A$,i,1)', since C$ is never declared anywhere in the program - flagged as a likely OCR/print error.
solution.ne: The FUNCTION COUNT(A$) is declared and defined but never called in the main module, and its result is never displayed. The missing statement, placed after the INPUT line, is 'PRINT COUNT(W$)', which calls the function with the entered word and prints the number of vowels it returns. Note: this answer also assumes the printed 'MID$(C$,i,1)' inside the function should read 'MID$(A$,i,1)', since C$ is never declared anywhere in the program - flagged as a likely OCR/print error.

items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION COUNT (A$)
CLS
INPUT "Enter any word";W$
PRINT COUNT(W$)
END

FUNCTION COUNT (A$)
  B=LEN(A$)
  C=0
FOR i=1 TO B
  E$=MID$(A$,i,1)
  IF E$="A" OR E$="E" OR E$="I" OR E$="O" OR E$="U" THEN
  C=C+1
  END IF
NEXT i
COUNT=C
END FUNCTION

title.en: Group C - Q8: Convert/Calculate as per the instruction
title.ne: Group C - Q8: Convert/Calculate as per the instruction

solution.en: Convert octal to decimal first: (1503)8 = 1x8^3 + 5x8^2 + 0x8^1 + 3x8^0 = 512 + 320 + 0 + 3 = 835 in decimal. Then convert 835 to hexadecimal by dividing repeatedly by 16: 835/16 = 52 remainder 3; 52/16 = 3 remainder 4; 3/16 = 0 remainder 3. Reading the remainders bottom-up gives (343)16.

Then convert 835 to hexadecimal by dividing repeatedly by 16: 835/16 = 52 remainder 3; 52/16 = 3 remainder 4; 3/16 = 0 remainder 3. Reading the remainders bottom-up gives (343)16.

solution.en: Group the 9-bit binary number into sets of 3 bits from the right: 101 000 101. Convert each group: 101 = 5, 000 = 0, 101 = 5, giving the octal number (505)8.

answer.en: A QBASIC program using a Function procedure for perimeter and a Sub procedure for volume, as shown in the code field.
answer.ne: A QBASIC program using a Function procedure for perimeter and a Sub procedure for volume, as shown in the code field.

solution.en: The main module takes the room's length (L), breadth (B), and height (H) as input. It calls the Function procedure Perimeter(L, B), which returns 2*(L+B), and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Volume(L, B, H) using CALL, which computes L*B*H internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.
solution.ne: The main module takes the room's length (L), breadth (B), and height (H) as input. It calls the Function procedure Perimeter(L, B), which returns 2*(L+B), and prints the result directly since a function returns a value. It then calls the Sub procedure Volume(L, B, H) using CALL, which computes L*B*H internally and prints it itself, since a sub does not return a value to the caller.

items.code:
DECLARE FUNCTION Perimeter (L, B)
DECLARE SUB Volume (L, B, H)

CLS
INPUT "Enter length of room: ", L
INPUT "Enter breadth of room: ", B
INPUT "Enter height of room: ", H

PRINT "Perimeter = "; Perimeter(L, B)
CALL Volume(L, B, H)

END

FUNCTION Perimeter (L, B)
    Perimeter = 2 * (L + B)
END FUNCTION

SUB Volume (L, B, H)
    V = L * B * H
    PRINT "Volume = "; V
END SUB

answer.en: A QBASIC program that reads student records from "std.dat" and displays only those with Computer marks greater than 40, as shown in the code field.
answer.ne: A QBASIC program that reads student records from "std.dat" and displays only those with Computer marks greater than 40, as shown in the code field.

solution.en: The file "std.dat" is opened FOR INPUT. A DO WHILE NOT EOF(1) loop reads one student's record at a time with INPUT #1 into the name, roll number, and the four subject marks. An IF condition checks whether the Computer marks (Comp) are greater than 40, and if so, prints that student's full record. The loop continues until the end of the file is reached, after which the file is closed. Assumption: the exact order and names of the fields stored in std.dat were not fully specified on the paper beyond 'name, roll no. and marks of English, Nepali, Maths, and Computer'; this order has been assumed - please verify against the original file layout if available.
solution.ne: The file "std.dat" is opened FOR INPUT. A DO WHILE NOT EOF(1) loop reads one student's record at a time with INPUT #1 into the name, roll number, and the four subject marks. An IF condition checks whether the Computer marks (Comp) are greater than 40, and if so, prints that student's full record. The loop continues until the end of the file is reached, after which the file is closed. Assumption: the exact order and names of the fields stored in std.dat were not fully specified on the paper beyond 'name, roll no. and marks of English, Nepali, Maths, and Computer'; this order has been assumed - please verify against the original file layout if available.

items.code:
OPEN "std.dat" FOR INPUT AS #1
CLS
PRINT "Students with marks in Computer > 40:"
DO WHILE NOT EOF(1)
    INPUT #1, SName$, RollNo, Eng, Nep, Maths, Comp
    IF Comp > 40 THEN
        PRINT SName$, RollNo, Eng, Nep, Maths, Comp
    END IF
LOOP
CLOSE #1
END
